extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, parties to PTAB/AIA proceedings, and other USPTO stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules governing requests for Director Review of PTAB decisions under the Leahy‑Smith America Invents Act (AIA), including who/what may be reviewed, timing/format of requests, effects on underlying proceedings, appeal timing, and delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Director Review - eligible decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to an AIA proceeding may request Director Review in that proceeding of any: decision on institution; final decision (defined as a final written decision in an inter partes or post grant review proceeding or a final decision in a derivation proceeding); decision granting rehearing of a decision on institution or a final decision; other decision concluding an AIA proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerates the categories of PTAB decisions that a party may seek rehearing of via Director Review; the page uses the final rule's exact categories and the statutory AIA proceeding context when listing eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may initiate review sua sponte
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule provides that the Director may initiate a review of such decisions on the Director’s own initiative (“sua sponte”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the Director independent authority to commence review without a party request; practitioners should account for potential sua sponte reviews when considering case strategy and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and format requirements for requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule sets forth the timing and format of a party’s request for Director Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the press release summarizes that timing and format are specified, practitioners must consult the full final rule for the precise deadlines, filing format, and any required form/content of requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Director Review on underlying PTAB proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule addresses the impact of Director Review on the underlying PTAB proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers how a Director Review interacts procedurally with the ongoing PTAB matter (e.g., stays, pauses, or continued action) — the summary indicates the issue is addressed but practitioners should review the rule text for detailed effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of timing to file appeal to the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule clarifies the time by which an appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This changes or clarifies appellate timing in cases involving Director Review; parties appealing a PTAB decision should confirm the clarified deadlines in the final rule to preserve appellate rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule provides that the Director may delegate a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's ability to delegate affects who will actually conduct the review; parties should be aware that delegated reviewers may act under delegated authority and consult the final rule for any limits or procedures relating to delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalization of interim Director Review process
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule formalizes key aspects of the interim Director Review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement notes the rule codifies practices previously in interim use; practitioners who relied on interim procedures should review how the final rule confirms or changes those practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of the final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule is effective on October 31, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All procedural changes and requirements summarized become operative on this date; filings and strategy should be planned accordingly.
